Our core problem: Agentic Tasks (0.420) and Instruction Following (0.477) remain our weakest scores and users rank agentic as their top priority. Mirage jumped +0.018 on Agentic this month alone — we're at risk of falling further behind. Function Calling (0.441) is similarly weak. These three areas need concentrated R&D focus.

Coding is stagnant at 0.579 with zero movement despite 'very high' priority — we're not getting returns there. Hard Coding, Advanced Math, Long Context, and Legal Reasoning are lower-user-priority areas where we're spending attention without clear ROI. Reallocating from these toward Agentic/IF/Function Calling is the right move.

Safety stays at current investment — our 0.608 score is competitive among mid-tier players, our red-teaming credibility is established, and the Orion collapse validates the open-source safety narrative. We don't need to outspend here, just maintain.

The Nvidia partnership is a product unlock — enterprise inference at scale is now live. Product spending holds steady to support this without over-indexing. Shifting R&D slightly higher captures the AGI-ready positioning we announced.
traces.Spark AI:
The market just reshuffled dramatically. Orion lost 28 points of share and Apex captured most of it on the back of safety credibility — but Apex's safety scores (0.809, 0.814) are now far above ours and likely unreachable without massive compute investment. Trying to compete on safety against Apex is a losing bet for a resource-constrained startup.

Instead, the Orion collapse creates a real opening for developer-focused customers who need strong agentic and coding capabilities. Our Agentic Tasks score (0.361) and Function Calling (0.383) are dangerously low — well below even Genesis and Mirage — and these directly map to user priorities #1 and #3 (agentic, communication). Coding remains our anchor but we're losing ground to Mirage (+0.023 this month alone).

User research now shows 'knowledge' as priority #1, which maps to General Capability and Instruction Following — both neglected. We should lift priority on those.

Safety spend can trim slightly: we've established credibility, the market now has multiple safety-credible players, and our Safety score is static. Redirecting that budget to R&D gives us more capacity to close the agentic/function calling gap.

Product/GTM stays the same — we need to be present to capture displaced Orion customers but shouldn't over-invest in GTM until our product scores are more competitive.

Deprioritize Scientific Reasoning, Clinical Reasoning, Legal Reasoning, Long Context, and Advanced Math — these don't map to user priorities and we have no differentiation angle.
